title: Polyploidization-Driven Functional Innovation of AGPase Small Subunit Gene APS1 Regulates Starch Biosynthesis in Banana (Musa acuminata).
authors: Sun, Junmei; Zhu, Zhao; Sun, Peiguang; Tu, Yunen; Hou, Xiaowan; Ali, Muhammad Moaaz; Jin, Yueruxin; Zhang, Min; Huang, Dongyi; Song, Xiqiang; Liu, Juhua; Jin, Zhiqiang; Miao, Hongxia
one_liner_zh: 该文研究香蕉AGPase小亚基APS1基因的多倍化功能分化与淀粉合成调控，虽涉及转录因子与启动子互作的分子对接预测，但核心是基因表达与功能验证，非TF-DNA互作机制建模，AI/物理模拟方法仅浅层应用。
abstract: Starch biosynthesis is a fundamental process influencing yield and fruit quality in banana, with ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase (AGPase) serving as the rate-limiting enzyme catalyzing sucrose conversion into starch. However, the mechanisms underlying functional differentiation of AGPase family genes following polyploidization remain largely unexplored. In this study, eight AGPase genes, including large (MaAPL) and small subunit (MaAPS) members, were identified from the banana (Musa acuminata) genome, all harboring the conserved ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase domain. Phylogenetic analysis traced their evolutionary origin to the ancient moss Physcomitrella patens, with polyploidization identified as the primary driver of gene family expansion. These genes exhibit conserved codon usage bias and have undergone strong purifying selection. Among them, MaAPS1 displayed distinct functional differentiation, increased intron number, enriched promoter cis-elements, and significantly elevated expression-features likely contributing to its adaptation for enhanced starch accumulation in fruit. Furthermore, the MaAPS1 protein was predominately localized in the chloroplast. Functional validation supported its regulatory involvement: transient silencing in banana fruit reduced starch content, while transient overexpression in banana fruit increased starch levels. Co-expression and molecular docking analyses revealed that transcription factors ERF1, C3H1, bZIP1, and bZIP3 may interact with the MaAPS1 promoter, indicating a multifactorial regulatory network. Overall, this study provides insights into polyploidy-driven functional innovation and transcriptional regulation of MaAPS1 in banana starch biosynthesis, providing valuable molecular targets for genetic improvement of yield and fruit quality.
abstract_zh: 淀粉生物合成是影响香蕉产量和果实品质的基础过程，其中ADP-葡萄糖焦磷酸化酶（AGPase）作为限速酶，催化蔗糖转化为淀粉。然而，多倍化后AGPase家族基因功能分化的机制仍 largely 未被探索。本研究从香蕉（Musa acuminata）基因组中鉴定出八个AGPase基因，包括大亚基（MaAPL）和小亚基（MaAPS）成员，所有基因均含有保守的ADP-葡萄糖焦磷酸化酶结构域。系统发育分析将其进化起源追溯至古老苔藓植物小立碗藓（Physcomitrella patens），并确定多倍化为基因家族扩张的主要驱动力。这些基因表现出保守的密码子使用偏好，并经历了强烈的纯化选择。其中，MaAPS1显示出明显的功能分化、内含子数量增加、启动子顺式元件富集以及显著升高的表达水平——这些特征可能有助于其适应果实中增强的淀粉积累。此外，MaAPS1蛋白主要定位于叶绿体。功能验证支持其调控作用：在香蕉果实中瞬时沉默降低淀粉含量，而瞬时过表达则增加淀粉水平。共表达和分子对接分析揭示，转录因子ERF1、C3H1、bZIP1和bZIP3可能与MaAPS1启动子相互作用，表明存在多因子调控网络。总体而言，本研究为香蕉淀粉生物合成中多倍化驱动的功能创新和MaAPS1的转录调控提供了见解，为产量和果实品质的遗传改良提供了有价值的分子靶点。
